utterances.text: Now this particular item, as we go to the last two lines, at this particular check-point it notes that the items were -- talking about these items, these items were handed over for safe-keeping and a military disciplinary report was filed. So these individuals at the check-point actually took these items. Is that right? The law enforcement?

utterances.speaker: VESELKO BILIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us go cover a couple of items. You noted, as we said previously in paragraph 4 of your statement, which is - we don't need to bring it up on the screen - D1547 that you were demobilised when you turned in your weapon on 18 August. And I would like to address you to a series of reports put into evidence by the Prosecution, and these are P2187, a report from the military police, dated 4 October. If I can, I'm just going to go through these documents very quickly and then just ask you one question. P2187, page 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I'm not quite certain about the purposes of showing a document to the witness. It is obviously in danger of being a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have two concerns: The first is that we hear from the witness the evidence he can give us, within the ordinary course of the proceedings; and I'm also looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can I just cut this short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please ask the question, and if there would be any need to further show documents to the witness, we will consider how to proceed and when to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Bilic, were you aware that initially your case was being jointly investigated by the military police and the MUP? And I'm talking about the murder of Dara Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: VESELKO BILIC
utterances.text: No, the civilian police did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And were you aware that there was a determination that you were not a member of the HV when you committed the murder of Dara Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: VESELKO BILIC
utterances.text: They didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, you were ultimately, as you noted, you went through the civilian courts; didn't you? Where you received your sentence of eight years.

utterances.speaker: VESELKO BILIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I can argue those documents at the appropriate time, Mr. President. I don't really think at this point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't whether the witness can shed some additional light on the prosecutorial and judicial competence. But if we have the documents, that matter can be argued on the basis of those documents, it seems to me at least. I'm also looking at the other Defence teams. Apparently no further questions. Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, the only issue I have -- would have two document I wanted to bar table, but we can do that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can do that. And I take it that we don't need the witness for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Bilic, this concludes your evidence in this court. I would like to thank you very much for coming a long way and for having answered questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench. And I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to thank you for handling this all right. I wanted to greet my generals and pass the greetings of all of Croatia. I cannot steer clear of that, and I can hardly wait for them to be back home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's not usual that you greet as a witness the accused, but, of course, the accused have heard that you intended to do that, and that message certainly reached them. Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Bilic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two - very quickly - one or two procedural matters. First, has the Prosecution been supplied with the witness statement for Witness AG-24 so as to enable them. If not, you're invited to take care that it happens.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. That -- I have been trying to get the Rule 70 clearance for some time, and I'm giving my best efforts to get the clearance, and it has not been a Rule 70 clear -- I will tell you that it's not very extensive, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that. But the only thing is that the Prosecution noted that it needs to see the statement before it can respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, I will tell that you I am in unison with their request to get --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think there's no --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can I -- I have been informed of one issue on that, and without going into the identity, the statement is virtually -- I don't want to say it's virtually identical, but consistent with the information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would not -- as a matter of fact, if there is anything to be said, then we can do that not in the time we have stolen already from interpreters, transcribers, the security officers, et cetera. There is one other matter, yes. We will not sit on the 6th of July, and the earlier you know that, I think the better it is. There are other matters, but we will leave them until tomorrow. We adjourn, and we resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 2nd of July, at quarter past 2.00, in Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 2nd day of July, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.07 p.m.,
